pr_title: Add min and max facet stats
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Related issue
Fixes #3426

## What does this PR do?

### User standpoint

- When using a `facets` parameter in search, the facets that have numeric values are displayed in a new section of the response called `facetStats` that contains, per facet, the numeric min and max value of the hits returned by the search.

Sample request/response
</summary>

issue_context.title: Return stats for numerical facets like `min`, `max`
issue_context.body:
Related product discussion: https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/117
Related specification: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/224
Also related to: https://github.com/meilisearch/instant-meilisearch/issues/926

### TODO

- [x] For implementation, check with the product squad to get how it should be implemented
    - A prototype PR with only `min` and `max` is available: #3423. Do we need `avg` and `sum`?
- [x] Merge the changes into main
- [x] Update the specification


### Impacted teams

@meilisearch/integration-team: usable for https://github.com/meilisearch/instant-meilisearch/issues/926
@meilisearch/docs-team

You can test it by using
-  the [release assets](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/releases)
- the [Meilisearch Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/getmeili/meilisearch/general)
```bash
docker run -it --rm -p 7700:7700 -v $(pwd)/meili_data:/meili_data getmeili/meilisearch:v1.1.0-rc.0
```

You are more than welcome to communicate any feedback about this new implementation in [this discussion](https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/117).
If you encountered any bugs, please report them [here](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/new?assignees=&labels=&template=bug_report.md&title=).
Thanks in advance for your help and your involvement in Meilisearch ❤️ 

🎉 Official and stable release containing this change will be available on 3rd April 2023

review_comments:
Is is possible for this condition to be false?
(Even if it is not, I am okay with keeping it, out of an excess of caution :) )

I really don't know, I used the same check as in the `execute` method of the same object, as it looked equally applicable (thinking of it maybe we should factor this code somehow 🤔?). According to git blame it was added as part of a commit titled `nested fields`, if that helps.

👍 
However, I don't really understand why we use an `impl Iterator` instead of `Box<dyn Iterator` now. Was that necessary in order to put a pointer to the DB key inside?

I'm honestly not sure anymore if it was necesssary, I believe I just changed it as part of my refactoring. I like to avoid allocations when practical, but that line is not always easy to find. I don't mind changing it back if you prefer.
